taken as written

explanation.definitionFit: Lightish means somewhat pale, so quite fair in complexion or colour.

clue.text: Devil flares up when struck

definitions.meaning: an old word for a friction match, which ignites when rubbed

explanation.definitionFit: Lucifer is both a name for Satan and an old term for a match struck to light.

explanation.walkthrough: The page splits 'retirement' across a line, so the definition reads 'retire ment wish'.

clue.text: Fellow with book coming in to recount Iris Murdoch story

explanation.definitionFit: Iris Murdoch wrote the novel The Bell, so it is one of her stories.

clue.text: Escape in this car, perhaps

explanation.definitionFit: To scarper is British slang for running away, to escape.

clue.text: It's a bullet, you idiot

definitions.meaning: a soft-nosed bullet that expands on impact

explanation.definitionFit: A dumdum is an expanding bullet, and in slang a dumdum is a fool.

clue.text: Head of department is taking English period, being free

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.definitionFit: To disengage is to release or detach, so to set free.

clue.text: Non-U greeting in early part of day

explanation.definitionFit: The morning is the early part of the day, before noon.

clue.text: Joanna's support

definitions.meaning: a vertical post holding something up

explanation.walkthrough: Joanna is Cockney rhyming slang for piano; an upright piano stands vertically.
explanation.definitionFit: An upright is a vertical piano and also a vertical post used as a support.

clue.text: Unite to make cabbies go out of business?

definitions.text: Unite to make cabbies go out of business?

parts.words: Unite to make cabbies go out of business?

explanation.definitionFit: To close ranks is an idiom for a group uniting in mutual defence.

clue.text: Scotsman's brief word of thanks spurned by charity organisation

parts.note: the Rotary is a charitable service club
ta is a short informal word for thanks

explanation.definitionFit: Rory is a typically Scottish man's name, so a Scotsman.

clue.text: Digitally-processed picture?

parts.note: digitally suggests computers, but digits are also fingers, so a picture made with the fingers

explanation.definitionFit: A painting made by applying paint with the fingers rather than brushes, often by children.

clue.text: Serviceman repulsed fighters with gun

parts.note: RA is the Royal Artillery, a body of fighters
a Luger is a German pistol

explanation.surface: A soldier drove back enemy troops with his weapon.
explanation.definitionFit: A regular is a professional soldier in a standing army, a serviceman.

clue.text: Companion interrupting a rude fellow

parts.note: ribald means coarsely rude

explanation.definitionFit: Archibald is a man's name, and crossword setters let a name define a fellow.

clue.text: Badly-behaved thug, after treatment, is in denial

parts.note: nay is an old word of denial

indicators.note: treatment processes the letters, rearranging them

explanation.definitionFit: Naughty describes a child or person behaving badly or disobediently.

clue.text: Power to twist cable

indicators.note: twist signals the letters are wrung into a new order

explanation.definitionFit: Perugia is a city in Umbria, central Italy.

explanation.definitionFit: Petrine means relating to St Peter, so belonging to that saint.

clue.text: Having phoned home, start to go travelling far and wide

parts.note: rang is the past of ring, to phone
in means at home

indicators.note: start to names the first letter of the word after it

explanation.surface: After calling home, someone sets off on a wide journey.
explanation.definitionFit: Ranging means roaming over a wide area.

clue.text: Confident lower classes will join country uprising, I left
